text:
nora: Heads-up — customer hit an odd case on RHEL9 where the HSM PKCS#11 plugin binds a unix socket in /tmp and the redwood service can't open it when SELinux is Enforcing + PrivateTmp. I opened a short docs PR with remediation steps and an air-gapped installer note: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4728

sam: can you paste the AVC denial so we capture the exact AV context?

nora: sure, extracted from audit.log: `May 18 09:23:10 host audit[3321]: AVC avc:  denied  { open } for pid=3321 comm=\"redwood-hsm\" name=pkcs11.sock scontext=system_u:system_r:redwood_t:s0 tcontext=unconfined_u:object_r:tmp_t:s0 tclass=unix_stream_socket`

aya: TL;DR: PrivateTmp causes the process to create sockets labelled tmp_t. redwood_t cannot open tmp_t. Docs should show two paths: preferred = persistent path under /var/lib/redwood with SELinux fcontext + restorecon at install; fallback = conservative systemd override to turn off PrivateTmp for the HSM unit.

nora: added this minimal systemd fragment example in the PR (keeps PrivateTmp but uses RuntimeDirectory):

`# /etc/systemd/system/redwood-hsm.service.d/10-persistent-socket.conf
[Service]
PrivateTmp=yes
RuntimeDirectory=redwood-hsm
RuntimeDirectoryMode=0755
ExecStartPre=/bin/mkdir -p /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket
ExecStartPre=/bin/chown redwood:redwood /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket || true
ExecStartPre=/usr/sbin/semanage fcontext -a -t var_run_t '/var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket(/.*)?' || true
ExecStartPre=/sbin/restorecon -R /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket || true
# plugin binds to /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket/pkcs11.sock`

sam: include a chcon fallback for minimal installs that lack semanage. Also add an explicit "do not suggest `setenforce 0`" line — security flagged that in other docs.

aya: added an AppArmor note for Ubuntu: append `/var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket/*` to the redwood-hsm profile and reload with `apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/usr.bin.redwood-hsm`. That should cover Debian/Ubuntu distros that don't use SELinux.

nora: PR includes a tiny migration script for existing on-prem customers that may have sockets still in /tmp. Kept it minimal for air-gapped installs — it only relies on coreutils/systemctl: `if [ -S /tmp/pkcs11.sock ]; then systemctl stop redwood-hsm; mkdir -p /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket; mv /tmp/pkcs11.sock /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket/; chown root:root /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket/pkcs11.sock; systemctl start redwood-hsm; fi`

sam: docs-bot: link-check flagged an internal KB url in the PR — removed the broken reference and updated to the internal KB canonical path.

docs-bot: Link-check: fail in PR 4728 — replaced `https://kb.redwood.internal/selinux-sockets-old` with `https://kb.redwood.internal/selinux-sockets` (manual approve required).

aya: wording suggestion for Troubleshooting FAQ: "If HSM socket access fails on systems with PrivateTmp, prefer creating a persistent socket directory with correct file context; if you cannot set file contexts during install (air-gapped minimal installs), use the chcon workaround and document the limitation." Keep it short and link to the Advanced SELinux section which contains semanage examples.

sam: Security note: remove semanage from the Quickstart page — keep it under Advanced > SELinux since semanage isn't installed on minimal images by default.

nora: done. I'll run the air-gap smoke test on a RHEL9 VM and report back here. Leaving thread open for test results and any tweak suggestions.
